changes.balance: The diplomatic channel moved the price without moving a barrel: a third day of talks and a two day reopening sequence took about 3 percent off both benchmarks from six month highs, while the loadings gauge west of Hormuz held at about 11 million barrels a day and no agreement exists. The move is a positioning print until a flow print or an accepted agreement makes it a supply print.
changes.body: Brent Jan27, the front contract from Monday, traded down to $109.75 in early Asian trade (QNA, Nov 2), down $3.68 or 3.2 percent from Friday's $113.43 settle, with the session's first Reuters print at $111.84; WTI Dec26 traded to $100.69, down $3.43 or 3.3 percent from $104.12, off a first Reuters print of $102.56. The $4.21 December to January Brent step is contract roll and is not part of the move. Iranian and Qatari officials held a third consecutive day of talks in Doha: the reopening proposal shortened from seven days to two, with Washington to act on the first day on sanctions relief, frozen funds release and oil waivers, and Qatar is pushing the release of more than $6 billion of frozen Iranian assets as the central step. Iran's foreign minister said Nov 1 the consultations had reached no conclusion and there are no plans for direct talks with Washington. December WCS is -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots, and November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The validated diesel crack is $90.90 on the Nov 2 print.
changes.conditional: An accepted agreement with terms published, or a tier one flow print stepping up from about 11 million barrels a day, would make the diplomatic channel a supply event. If the talks stall and the price does not recover toward the $113.43 January settle, the overnight move was positioning rather than a talks effect.
changes.delta: Overnight: Brent Jan27 $109.75 at the low Asian print (QNA, Nov 2), down $3.68 from Friday's $113.43 settle; WTI Dec26 $100.69, down $3.43. Doha talks day three, two day reopening proposal, frozen funds release of more than $6 billion as the centrepiece, no conclusion per Iran's foreign minister Nov 1. December WCS -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots. ARV to TMW December spread +$6.99. Diesel crack $90.90 on the validated history. November apportionment Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert in effect.
changes.source: QNA and Reuters, Nov 2, 2026; Reuters, Gulf News and Guardian reporting, Nov 1-2, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 30, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Nov 2, 2026; Enbridge apportionment notice, Oct 20, 2026
changes.title: Crude sold off about 3 percent on a third day of Doha talks, and the Canadian front carries Friday's traded tightening into the reporting week

changes.balance: The group's ceiling is held and is not supply: most members pump below target, so the formal hold changes no December barrels, and the group's real decision is the 2027 framework on Nov 29, where the capacity review sets the baselines the quotas are built on.
changes.body: The seven core members' statement after Sunday's online meeting formalised the decision carried in principle on Nov 1: maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026, a third straight monthly hold, at a combined target of about 31.01 million barrels a day (Saudi Arabia 10.478, Russia 9.949, Iraq 4.431, Kuwait 2.676, Kazakhstan 1.628, Algeria 1.007, Oman 0.841). The phased rollback of a 1.65 million barrel a day cut completed in September, and a further layer of about 2 million barrels a day of cuts runs through the end of 2026. Saudi Arabia told OPEC it produced 8.372 million barrels a day in September, more than 2 million under its December target. The group next meets Nov 29 to decide the 2027 framework.
changes.conditional: The Nov 29 ministerial is the next decision point: a 2027 framework built on revised capacity baselines would change the group's supply path; the December hold itself does not.
changes.delta: OPEC+ statement Nov 1 formalised the December hold at September levels, combined target about 31.01 Mb/d for the seven core members, third straight monthly hold. Next meeting Nov 29 on the 2027 framework.
changes.source: OPEC+ statement via wire reporting, Nov 1, 2026
changes.title: OPEC+ formalised the December hold, and the 2027 framework decision is dated Nov 29

changes.balance: The reserve programme is fully awarded and unchanged since Friday's check, so its remaining content is scheduling: deliveries out through December, and from early next year the return of more than 216 million barrels, 44 million of it premium barrels. The one open item is the heating oil reserve exchange, whose delivery deadline is Nov 13 with no award document posted.
changes.body: Checked directly on Nov 2, the Energy Department's newest reserve item remains the Oct 29 announcement completing the 172 million barrel commitment, and no new solicitation, award or changed award sheet has posted since the Oct 31 check. The two completed sales stand as corrected on Oct 31: FY27 Sale No. 1 awarded 16,750,000 barrels of 17 million offered, and FY26 Sale No. 4 awarded 23,800,000 barrels of 40 million offered, 40.55 million combined. No award document has been posted for the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange; deliveries under it are due by Nov 13.
changes.conditional: A posted heating oil reserve award closes the last open reserve item. Any change to the posted award sheets, or a delivery schedule from the Department, updates the return timing.
changes.delta: No change since the Oct 31 direct check: newest reserve item remains the Oct 29 announcement; award sheets unchanged; heating oil reserve award still not posted (positive read of the award pages, Nov 2).
changes.source: US Department of Energy newsroom and Award Information sheets, checked directly Nov 2, 2026
changes.title: Reserves: a direct check on Nov 2 finds no new posting, and the heating oil award remains open

flags.body: Iranian and Qatari officials held a third day of talks in Doha on Nov 1-2. The reopening proposal shortened from seven days to two: Washington acts on the first day on sanctions relief, the release of frozen funds and restored oil waivers, and shipping resumes on the second. Qatar is pushing the release of more than $6 billion of frozen Iranian assets as the central step. Iran's foreign minister said Nov 1 the consultations had reached no conclusion and there are no plans for direct talks with Washington; Washington has said no decision has been made on renewed strikes. Crude sold off about 3 percent in early Asian trade Monday. Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed two tankers hit mines on an unauthorised route through the strait (Gulf News, Nov 2), with no vessel named and no CENTCOM or UKMTO confirmation reported. Preliminary October loadings west of Hormuz ran about 11 Mb/d against 14.5 before the war (Vortexa via Windward, Oct 29). Trade the loadings, not the claim count.
flags.title: Hormuz: a third day of Doha talks, a two day reopening proposal with no acceptance, and an unconfirmed mine claim
flags.trigger: A published agreement with accepted terms, a tier one flow print stepping away from about 11 Mb/d in either direction, or a confirmed vessel strike with an owner or UKMTO report

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. December's outlook opens at persistence on those levels. The evidence pack for a December call includes Friday's traded December tightening (990 lots at -$29.75), the export spread's compression through $7, Imperial's reported volumes, the November maintenance overlap at the mining complex and Kearl, and an overnight flat price slide that touched no Canadian physical fact. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; an unregistered call after that date is a lost data point for the prediction record.
flags.title: December apportionment: the nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7, no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: Registration of a December judgment call, the Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop

flags.body: Monday's front month Brent is the January contract, which settled at $113.43 on Friday against the expiring December contract's $117.64. The $4.21 difference is the contract roll and the expiry backwardation. Monday's overnight fall, to $109.75 at the low Asian print, is measured against the January settle and is a real move of about 3 percent; read any Monday settle against $113.43, not against December's expiry print.
flags.title: Brent front month rolled on Monday: read the overnight fall against the January settle of $113.43
flags.trigger: Monday's January Brent settle, read against Friday's $113.43 January settle
